meta.triageRationale: One cohesive capability with real design choices and several build tasks, built on parts that already exist (per-repo tracker config, three automatic pushes, an unwired issue-create function).

findings.premise: Every tracked kind in the user's decision (c10: issue, story, tasks) is designed, including the tasks of a standalone story: 'A PLAN pushes its tasks (autoPushTasksOnPlan) whenever the setting is on', and a BUILD approval closes 'each task issue in the plan's meta.tracker.taskRefs'.
findings.evidence: autoPushTasksOnPlan (tracker-auto.ts:262-264) does `try { define = readDefineArtifact(repoPath, epicHash); } catch (err) { return { status: 'failed', reason: `cannot read parent Define: ...` }; }`, and readDefineArtifact (gates.ts:119-126) reads only `DEF-<epicHash>.json` and throws ArtifactMissingError otherwise. A standalone work item has no DEF: this very item has only `.insrc/artifacts/LLD-38436e90625a83a2-S001.json`. The design itself says autoPushStoryOnLld 'reads the parent Define, so it cannot serve a standalone story' but gives the PLAN no standalone branch. The function also takes the parent story ref from the Define's storyRefs or the LLD's storyRef (lines 266-272), so a standalone story that only commented on its issue record's GitHub issue has no parent ref either. Result: every standalone or bugfix-sized plan approval returns 'failed', and no task issues exist for the BUILD approval to close. [files: src/workflow/tracker-auto.ts, src/workflow/gates.ts]
findings.action: Give the PLAN kind the same split as the LLD kind: for a plan with no parent Define, the tracker step creates the task issues itself (title, body and task id without define.meta.createdAt), with the parent taken from the LLD's storyRef or the issue record's issueRef. Add a test for a standalone PLAN.

findings.premise: Today only the TUI approve service pushes (HLD, LLD under an epic, PLAN) and commits; approveWorkflowTarget pushes nothing.
findings.evidence: src/cli/services/workflow.ts:161-166 is the only non-test call site of autoPushEpicOnHld / autoPushStoryOnLld / autoPushTasksOnPlan, followed by commitApprovedArtifacts. gates.ts:800-802 says of approveWorkflowTarget: 'Stamp-only: it does NOT run the tracker (gh-push/commit) leg', and its body (804-872) has no tracker call.

findings.premise: approve() in the TUI service is synchronous, typed in src/cli/services/index.ts:55, with two production callers that use the result synchronously (command.ts:223, WorkflowsPane.tsx:116).
findings.evidence: workflow.ts:156 `export function approve(artifactPath: string, withTracker = true, overrideReview?: string): ApproveOutcome`; index.ts:55 declares the same return type. command.ts:223 reads `r.approval.workflow` and `r.tracker.status` inside the already-async runWorkflow. WorkflowsPane.tsx:113-124 `doApprove = (item): void => { try { const r = svc.workflow.approve(item.path); ui.toast(...) ... refresh(); } catch ...` is synchronous and must become async with its try/catch and refresh moved after the await. Not in the design's inventory: the synchronous stubs in src/cli/__tests__/command.test.ts:50,223,234 and tui.test.ts:72.
findings.action: Add the two CLI test files' approve stubs to the change sites.

findings.premise: createBugfixTrackerIssue is not reached from any approval today, and the bugfix follow-on in mount.ts owns a close leg that reports 'bugfix-complete'.
findings.evidence: The only references to createBugfixTrackerIssue outside its own file are the re-export in bugfix/index.ts and the optional `opts.tracker` branch in advance.ts:66, which mount.ts never supplies (mount.ts:25-28: 'The GH-issue create leg is NOT injected here'). mount.ts:156-167 runs completeBugfixTracker for a BUILD carrying meta.issueHash and pushes kind 'bugfix-complete'; gates.ts:757 types that kind.
findings.action: When the close leg is removed, also narrow FollowOnOutcome.kind in gates.ts:757.

findings.premise: The three existing push functions can be reused with 'signatures and behaviour' unchanged while a repo with no github.json entry is tracked by default and a PLAN pushes with pushTasks false (T7: 'each call the existing push ... a PLAN pushes its tasks with pushTasks false').
findings.evidence: All three functions go through the private `gate()` (tracker-auto.ts:84-96), which calls `resolveGithubConfig(repoPath)` directly, with no injection, and returns `{ status: 'skipped', reason: 'tracker disabled via config (source: ...)' }` when `cfg.type === 'none'`. The design keeps resolveGithubConfig returning `{ type: 'none', source: 'default-config' }` for a repo with no entry (github.ts:213). So for the default-on repo the step's own checks pass and the delegated push then skips. autoPushTasksOnPlan also has `if (!cfg.pushTasks) return { status: 'skipped', reason: 'task push disabled ...' }` (255-257). gate() also calls ghAuthOk() itself, so the combined 'gh missing or not signed in' reason and a second auth call remain. The functions take their labels and issue types (cfg.epicLabel, cfg.storyIssueType, ...) from the same resolved config, which does not exist for a 'none' repo. [files: src/workflow/tracker-auto.ts, src/workflow/config/github.ts]
findings.action: State that the three functions change: they take the resolved target and labels (and no pushTasks gate) from the tracker step instead of calling gate(), and the step builds a full github-shaped config (default labels and issue types) from the git remote. Drop 'keep their behaviour' from the compatibility section and update T7.

findings.premise: The dynamic-key pattern of models.byRepo carries tracker.byRepo.<repoPath>.addItems: config.write accepts it and the boot-time reconcile does not strip it.
findings.evidence: The config.write handler (daemon/index.ts:1457-1481) takes `path: string | string[]` and calls setConfigAtPath with no catalog validation; write-path.ts uses array segments verbatim, so a repo path with dots and slashes is one key. reconcile.ts fills catalog rows and prunes only RETIRED_PATHS ('preserve every un-catalogued key EXCEPT those explicitly on the retired list'), so tracker.byRepo survives while the tracker.addItems row is filled with its default. The plugin writers are hard-wired as stated: repo-config.ts:154 `deps.writeKeyPath(['models', 'byRepo', write.repoPath, ...write.segments], ...)` and SettingsView.kt:720 `listOf("models", "byRepo", repoPath)`.

findings.premise: A work item's issue record is 'the ISSUE artifact with the same hash', so a BUILD record's or LLD's epicHash names the ISSUE whose ref is to be commented on or closed.
findings.evidence: storage.ts:358 resolves a work item's definition with `for (const artifactId of [defineArtifactId(epicHash), issueArtifactId(epicHash)])`, and tracker/resolve.ts:175 does the same with `DEF-${epicHash}.json` / `ISSUE-${epicHash}.json`. readRecordedRefFromDisk (bugfix/tracker.ts:378-383) reads meta.tracker.issueRef off `ISSUE-<hash>.json`, so calling closeBugfixTrackerIssue with issueHash = the BUILD's epicHash finds the ref. The close's default deps resolve config through resolveGithubConfig (tracker.ts:447), so the step must inject its own resolveConfig there too.
findings.action: Say explicitly that the step injects its own resolveConfig into both the create and close deps; with the defaults a default-on repo is skipped as 'no tracker configured'.

findings.premise: resolveGithubConfig 'has three other callers' outside the tracker step (cli/services/workflow.ts:97, questions.ts:474, tracker/sync.ts:36) and none needs to change.
findings.evidence: There are nine call sites. Beyond the three named: tracker-auto.ts:87 (gate), bugfix/tracker.ts:423 and :447 (default create and close deps), and runners/tracker/context.ts:41, :114, :144 (`requireGithubAdapter(resolveGithubConfig(ctx.intent.repoPath), ...)` for tracker.push, tracker.sync and tracker.post). The design says those three workflows 'remain for an explicit re-push or sync', but for a repo tracked by default with no github.json entry they still resolve 'none' and refuse, and syncTracker (sync.ts:37) returns 'tracker disabled via config'. So items the daemon pushed can be neither re-pushed nor synced. One of the three named callers, workflow.ts:97, sits inside commitApprovedArtifacts, which the design removes. [files: src/workflow/runners/tracker/context.ts, src/workflow/bugfix/tracker.ts, src/workflow/tracker/sync.ts, src/cli/services/workflow.ts]
findings.action: List all nine call sites and decide each. At minimum route the tracker.* runners and syncTracker through the tracker step's target lookup (setting, then entry or git remote), or state that explicit push and sync still need a github.json entry.

findings.premise: approveWorkflowTarget's callers need no change: the daemon handler already awaits it and its result reaches insrc_workflow_approve intact.
findings.evidence: gates.ts:804 is already `export async function approveWorkflowTarget(...)`. daemon/index.ts:652 awaits it and returns `result` or `{ ...result, followOn }`. mcp/server.ts:1105-1111 returns `JSON.stringify(result, null, 2)`, so a new tracker[] field passes through. The handler is at daemon/index.ts:643 as cited. Inside, approveOne is a synchronous closure (gates.ts:813) that must become async and awaited in both branches. The handler's early return at :667 (`result.approved.length === 0 || repoPath.length === 0`) does not affect a tracker step run inside approveWorkflowTarget, but a single-path approval can arrive with repoPath '' so the step must take the repo from the artifact's meta.repoPath.
findings.action: Note that the step reads repoPath from the artifact meta, not from req.repoPath.

findings.premise: A 'one-time step at daemon start' writes addItems=false for repos whose github.json entry says type 'none', and afterwards 'turning the setting on later tracks the repo'.
findings.evidence: The design names no record that the step has run. The only existing one-time mechanism, CONFIG_MIGRATIONS in reconcile.ts:319-329, moves a path inside config.json when `hasPath(config, fromKeys) && !hasPath(config, toKeys)`; it cannot read github.json. A step that 'writes false for every repo whose github.json entry says type none' at each daemon start passes T25 ('changes nothing on a second run') by being idempotent, yet rewrites false over a value the user later set to true, because the github.json entry still says 'none'. The same applies to the default entry and the catalog value. [files: src/config/reconcile.ts, src/config/config-catalog.ts]
findings.action: Specify the guard: write only when tracker.byRepo.<repo>.addItems is absent (and for the default, record a marker key such as tracker.migratedFromGithubJson). Add a test: a user sets true after migration, the daemon restarts, the value stays true.

findings.premise: Looking the unique label up before any create (ghFindIssueByLabels) means an issue whose ref was lost 'is never created twice'.
findings.evidence: github.ts:215-221: `try { num = out('gh', args); } catch { return undefined; }` and `return /^\d+$/.test(num) ? buildRef(...) : undefined`. Any lookup failure (rate limit, network error, the new 30 second timeout) is indistinguishable from 'no such issue', so the step goes on to create a second issue. The design's error table has no row for a failed lookup. The existing epic adoption (tracker-auto.ts:123) has the same weakness, but the design's guarantee and the backfill's 'safe to run twice' rest on it. [files: src/workflow/tracker/github.ts]
findings.action: Give the lookup a result that separates 'not found' from 'lookup failed', and make a failed lookup a 'failed' outcome with no create. Add the row to the error table and a test.

findings.premise: Failures of the gh calls are detectable as described: a 30 second timeout can be added at the one exec seam, gh-missing can be told apart from not-signed-in, and a create failure in the issue-record function surfaces as 'failed'.
findings.evidence: Every gh and git call goes through `out()` / `silent()` (github.ts:33-40), which pass an options object to `_exec` (execFileSync), so a `timeout` option is one change there and tests can simulate it through _setTrackerExecForTests. ghAuthOk (111-118) returns the single reason 'gh CLI not available or not authenticated', as the design says. createBugfixTrackerIssue has no 'failed' status: a gh failure during create throws ('A gh CLI failure DURING create ... propagates', tracker.ts:139-140) and issue-not-found throws (:164), so the 'failed' outcome exists only through the try/catch the design puts around the step. ghCreateIssueTyped retries untyped after any error of the typed call (164-170), so a timed-out typed call is followed by a second call.
findings.action: State that the step's own try/catch (not only approveWorkflowTarget's) maps a thrown create into 'failed', and that a timeout is not retried untyped.

findings.premise: T29: the existing approval suites can be given 'a temp config path' by one shared helper so they 'read no real config'.
findings.evidence: The setting lives in ~/.insrc/config.json, whose path is fixed: paths.ts:9 `config: join(INSRC_DIR, 'config.json')`, and the file has no process.env read. Only github.json has an override (github.ts:142 INSRC_GITHUB_CONFIG). The design's reader takes the path as a parameter, reachable only through `opts.tracker` of approveWorkflowTarget. Suites that reach the approval indirectly (the listed src/mcp/build-step tests, bugfix-orchestration) cannot pass that option, so a helper has nothing global to install, and the setting check, which runs first, reads the developer's real config. The gh side is fine: `_setTrackerExecForTests` exists (github.ts:29). [files: src/shared/paths.ts, src/workflow/config/github.ts]
findings.action: Add an env override for the config path (mirroring INSRC_GITHUB_CONFIG) or a module-level test seam for the setting reader, and name it in the helper.

findings.premise: The nine suites T29 names exist, and each acceptance criterion maps to at least one test.
findings.evidence: Glob finds all nine: src/workflow/__tests__/approve-workflow-target, approve-codereview-gate, approve-build-completion, approve-build-record-completion, other-party-review-gate, bugfix-orchestration; src/mcp/build-step/__tests__/build-start and build-step; src/workflow/runners/build/__tests__/build-record. The acceptance table maps ac1 to ac6 to T1-T29. Not covered: a standalone PLAN, a failed label lookup, and a restart after the user re-enables a migrated repo (see the findings above). T7 as written ('call the existing push ... with pushTasks false') cannot pass against the unchanged functions.
findings.action: Add the three missing tests and reword T7 once the push functions' change is specified.

summary.prose: One setting, "Add items to tracker", turns tracker pushing on or off for a repo. It is on by default and is shown on the VS Code and JetBrains settings pages. When it is on and the gh tool is installed and signed in, the daemon itself adds or updates the GitHub item each time a workflow item is approved, whichever way the approval was made, and commits and pushes the documents that item refers to. An issue record becomes a GitHub issue, an epic, its stories and its tasks are pushed, a standalone story gets its own issue, and approving a build closes the issue and its tasks. The approval result and the workflow's own messages say what was done or why nothing was, and the model in the session no longer runs gh. A backfill adds the approved items that were never pushed, and closes the finished ones at once.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Add an "Add items to tracker" setting and have the daemon log every workflow item to the tracker

api.name: approveWorkflowTarget
api.signature: approveWorkflowTarget(req: WorkflowApproveRequest, opts?: { enforce?: boolean; tracker?: TrackerStepDeps }): Promise<WorkflowApproveResult>

parameters.name: req
parameters.purpose: Unchanged: one artifact path or an epic hash, the repo path, and an optional override reason.

parameters.name: opts.tracker
parameters.purpose: Test seam for the tracker step (the setting reader, the gh check and the gh calls). Defaults to the real ones.

returns.meaning: As today, plus a new optional field tracker[]: one TrackerOutcome per approved artifact that is a tracker item. TrackerOutcome is ONE new type used on every path: { path, item: 'issue' | 'epic' | 'story' | 'tasks' | 'completion', status: 'created' | 'updated' | 'already-exists' | 'closed' | 'skipped' | 'failed', ref?, reason?, docs?: { committed: boolean; pushed: boolean; reason?: string } }. The existing result types are mapped into it: AutoPushResult's four statuses map one to one; the issue-record function's 'reused' maps to 'already-exists'; its 'created' with reason 'ref-unrecorded' maps to 'failed' and carries the created ref.

errors.condition: A tracker step that is skipped or fails never fails or undoes the approval; it is reported in tracker[] with its reason.

preconditions: Declared in src/workflow/gates.ts. Called by the daemon's 'workflow.approve' handler (src/daemon/index.ts:643), which serves insrc_workflow_approve and the plugins.
postconditions: For each artifact it approves, it awaits the tracker step once, AFTER the approval stamp is written, one artifact after another, never in parallel.
An artifact that was withheld (in skipped[]) gets no tracker step.
The tracker step is the only place that decides what a given approval adds to, updates on, or closes on the tracker; no caller chooses a push by itself.
Its callers are unchanged in how they call it: the daemon's 'workflow.approve' handler already awaits it.

api.name: approve
api.signature: approve(artifactPath: string, withTracker?: boolean, overrideReview?: string): Promise<ApproveOutcome>

parameters.name: withTracker
parameters.purpose: Unchanged meaning: false suppresses the tracker step for this call.

returns.meaning: CHANGED: it becomes asynchronous, because the tracker step awaits the issue-record functions, which are asynchronous. ApproveOutcome.tracker changes type from AutoPushResult to TrackerOutcome. ApproveOutcome.commit is removed: the commit and push of the documents is now part of the tracker step and is reported in TrackerOutcome.docs.

preconditions: Declared in src/cli/services/workflow.ts:156 and typed in the service interface at src/cli/services/index.ts:55. It is synchronous today and has two callers that use its result synchronously: src/cli/command.ts:223 and src/cli/panes/WorkflowsPane.tsx:116.
postconditions: Its own switch over the three pushes and its own commitApprovedArtifacts call are replaced by one awaited call to the shared tracker step.
Both callers are changed to await it: the command in src/cli/command.ts and doApprove in src/cli/panes/WorkflowsPane.tsx, and the interface in src/cli/services/index.ts declares the Promise.
withTracker false still suppresses the tracker step, including its commit and push.

api.name: autoPushStoryOnLld

returns.meaning: Unchanged, for a story under an epic. It is NOT given the standalone case: a standalone story is handled by the tracker step itself, so AutoPushResult keeps its four statuses.

preconditions: Declared in src/workflow/tracker-auto.ts:165. It reads the parent Define, so it cannot serve a standalone story; the tracker step does not call it for one.
postconditions: Called by the tracker step for an LLD that has a parent Define. A second approval of the same LLD creates nothing: the stored ref makes it 'already-exists'.

api.name: createBugfixTrackerIssue
api.signature: createBugfixTrackerIssue(input: { repoPath: string; issueHash: string }, deps: TrackerCreateDeps): Promise<TrackerIssueResult>

returns.meaning: Unchanged signature and result type. It is now reached: the tracker step awaits it when an issue record is approved, with labels supplied (see the tracker step), where today its default dependencies pass no labels.

preconditions: Declared in src/workflow/bugfix/tracker.ts:142. Not reached from any approval today (src/workflow/bugfix/mount.ts).
postconditions: Its existing rule holds: a ref already on the issue record's meta.tracker means the GitHub issue exists and none is created.
New, before any create: the tracker step looks the issue up on GitHub by the record's own label and adopts it when found, so an issue whose ref was lost is never created twice.

closeBugfixTrackerIssue is awaited by the tracker step when the work item's BUILD record is approved. It is no longer called from the bugfix follow-on in src/workflow/bugfix/mount.ts: the close has one owner.

api.name: resolveGithubConfig

returns.meaning: UNCHANGED, including its implicit default of type 'none' when github.json has no entry. The first draft of this design changed that default; it is withdrawn, because this function has three other callers that would change behaviour with it: the TUI's commit of artifacts (src/cli/services/workflow.ts:97), the question-resolution comment (src/workflow/questions.ts:474) and the tracker sync (src/workflow/tracker/sync.ts:36). The default-on behaviour lives in the tracker step's own target lookup instead.

preconditions: Declared in src/workflow/config/github.ts. Its callers outside the tracker step are src/cli/services/workflow.ts:97, src/workflow/questions.ts:474 and src/workflow/tracker/sync.ts:36; none of them changes.
postconditions: The owner and repo still never come from the default entry, only from the repo's own entry or its git remote.
The tracker step reads this function for the target and the label names only. It does not read the entry's type, pushTasks or commitArtifacts to decide whether to push: the one setting decides.

dataModelChanges.details: ONE flag turns tracker pushing on or off for a repo; nothing else does. A catalog row: path tracker.addItems, type boolean, default true, label "Add items to tracker", in a Tracker group; it is the value for any repo that has none of its own. A repo's own value is stored in the same config file under tracker.byRepo.<repoPath>.addItems, the dynamic-key pattern models.byRepo already uses. One reader returns the value for a repo: the repo's own value when present, otherwise the catalog value, otherwise true. The reader takes the config file's path as a parameter (defaulting to the real one) so a test can point it at a temp file. The flag replaces three older switches for the tracker step: an entry's type 'none', pushTasks and commitArtifacts in ~/.insrc/github.json are no longer read to decide whether to push. So that nobody who opted out is opted back in, a one-time step at daemon start writes tracker.byRepo.<repoPath>.addItems = false for every repo whose github.json entry says type 'none', and writes the catalog value false when the default entry says type 'none'. Settings pages. A catalog row reaches VS Code as a global key (vscode-plugin/src/config/key-map.ts maps every catalog path to 'insrc.' + path), which is the right place for the default. The per-repo value is shown and written in each plugin's per-repo section, whose writers are hard-wired to models.byRepo today: vscode-plugin/src/panels/repo-config.ts:154 and the base path in jetbrains-plugin/src/main/kotlin/ai/insors/insrc/jetbrains/settings/SettingsView.kt:720. Both are extended to write tracker.byRepo.<repoPath>.addItems for the open project. Each page labels the two plainly: the default for all repos, and this repo's value. The VS Code plugin also declares the setting in its package.json.

One asynchronous function in src/workflow/tracker-auto.ts that takes an approved artifact's json path and returns one TrackerOutcome, or none for a kind that is not tracked. CHECKS, in this order, each returning 'skipped' with its own reason: (1) the setting for the repo is true; (2) a GitHub target is found: the repo's entry in github.json when it names an owner and repo, otherwise the repo's git remote; (3) the gh tool is installed; (4) gh is signed in. The target is checked before gh so that a repo with no GitHub remote, which is every temp repo in the test suites, never runs gh. Finding the tool is separate from sign-in so the reason says which is missing; today's one check, ghAuthOk, reports both as one. BY KIND. An ISSUE record creates a GitHub issue (createBugfixTrackerIssue) carrying the label insrc:issue and a label unique to the record, insrc:issue-<first 8 of its hash>; before creating, the step looks that unique label up (ghFindIssueByLabels) and adopts the issue when it exists. An HLD pushes the epic and its stories (autoPushEpicOnHld). An LLD with a parent Define pushes the story (autoPushStoryOnLld). A standalone LLD: when the work item's issue record (the ISSUE artifact with the same hash) has a tracker ref, a comment linking the design is added to that GitHub issue and the outcome is 'updated'; otherwise one GitHub issue is created for the story from the LLD's title and summary, with the story label and a unique label insrc:story-<first 8 of the hash>-<story id>, and its ref is stored on the LLD's meta.tracker.storyRef. A PLAN pushes its tasks (autoPushTasksOnPlan) whenever the setting is on; pushTasks no longer gates it. A BUILD record closes what the Story opened: the GitHub issue of the work item's issue record (closeBugfixTrackerIssue), else the story issue on the LLD's meta.tracker.storyRef, and each task issue in the plan's meta.tracker.taskRefs; the refs are found from the BUILD record's epicHash and storyId, which name the ISSUE, LLD and PLAN artifacts. DEF, SPEC, CR and EXT give no outcome. DOCUMENTS. After the item is added or updated, the step commits and pushes the documents it refers to, with the existing commitAndPushArtifacts: the approved artifact's json and markdown, and the work item's definition alongside, as the TUI does today. It commits only those paths, on the current branch, and reports the result in TrackerOutcome.docs; a commit or push that fails does not change the item's status. This is the commit the TUI made in commitApprovedArtifacts; that function is removed. ONE CLOSE OWNER. The bugfix follow-on in src/workflow/bugfix/mount.ts no longer closes the issue: its completeBugfixTracker leg and the 'bugfix-complete' entry it put in followOn are removed, and the advance leg stays. TIME. Every gh and git call the step makes gets a timeout of 30 seconds; today they are blocking calls with none (src/workflow/tracker/github.ts:25). A call that passes it is a 'failed' outcome with the reason 'gh timed out'. The calls stay blocking, so the daemon serves no other request while one runs: an issue record is 2 to 3 calls, an epic about 10, typically 1 to 2 seconds each. The backfill yields to the event loop between items so other requests are served between them.

dataModelChanges.entity: What the workflow says about the tracker
dataModelChanges.details: Three places. (1) The result of insrc_workflow_approve carries tracker[], and its description says the daemon adds or updates the tracker item and pushes its documents on approval, and that the model must not run gh or commit the artifacts for it. (2) The done response of insrc_workflow_step: its pendingApproval block, built in src/mcp/workflow-step/phases/synthesize.ts:109 and typed in src/mcp/workflow-step/types.ts:129, gains a tracker line saying what approving this artifact will do: the target it will be added to, or why it will not be (setting off, no GitHub target, gh missing, gh not signed in, or a kind that is not tracked). The line is worked out by the same checks as the tracker step, without changing anything. (3) The steering source src/prompts/steering-block.md and its plugin copy vscode-plugin/assets/steering-block.md: the tracker guide and the bugfix guide say that tracking happens in the daemon at approval, which items are tracked and when, that the one setting and the gh tool control it, that a build approval closes the issue and its tasks, and that the model relays the tracker outcome and never pushes by hand; the tracker.push, tracker.sync and tracker.post workflows remain for an explicit re-push or sync.

A daemon stream request that takes a repo and a dry-run flag. It lists every approved artifact that is a tracker item and carries no tracker ref (approved issue records, approved HLDs, approved LLDs, approved plans), in an order that creates parents before children, and returns the list when the dry-run flag is set. Without the flag it runs the same tracker step on each, one at a time, yielding to the event loop between items and sending one progress frame per item, and ends with one outcome per item. An item whose BUILD record is already approved is created and then closed at once, so finished work does not show as open. Items not yet approved are not pushed; they are pushed when they are approved. It is safe to run twice: an item that already has a ref, or that is found on GitHub by its unique label, is reported as already there.

errorCases.scenario: The gh tool is not installed.
errorCases.detection: The tracker step looks for the gh executable before it calls it.
errorCases.response: The outcome is 'skipped' with the reason 'gh is not installed'. The approval stands.
errorCases.userImpact: The approval result and the workflow step's message say the item was not added and why.

errorCases.scenario: gh is installed but not signed in.
errorCases.detection: The existing sign-in check, gh auth status, exits non-zero.
errorCases.response: The outcome is 'skipped' with the reason 'gh is not signed in (run gh auth login)'. The approval stands.
errorCases.userImpact: The user is told to sign in; the item can be added later by the backfill.

errorCases.scenario: The repo has no GitHub remote and no target in the tracker config.
errorCases.detection: The step's target lookup finds no owner and repo in the repo's github.json entry and no GitHub remote.
errorCases.response: The outcome is 'skipped' with that reason, before any gh call. The approval stands.
errorCases.userImpact: The user is told no GitHub target could be found for the repo.

errorCases.scenario: A gh call fails while creating or updating the item (network, permissions, rate limit, a label or issue type the organisation does not have).
errorCases.detection: The gh call exits non-zero, or the push function returns status 'failed'.
errorCases.response: The outcome is 'failed' with gh's message. Nothing is retried in the same approval. The approval stands, and no tracker ref is written, so a later approval of the same artifact or the backfill tries again.
errorCases.userImpact: The approval result says the tracker step failed and why; the item is approved but not on the tracker.

errorCases.scenario: A gh or git call hangs (a stalled network, a credential prompt).
errorCases.detection: The call passes its 30 second timeout and is stopped.
errorCases.response: The outcome is 'failed' with the reason 'gh timed out' (or 'git timed out' for the documents). Nothing is retried in the same approval; the approval stands.
errorCases.userImpact: The approval returns after at most the timeout for that call; the daemon is not left frozen.

errorCases.scenario: The item was added but its documents could not be committed or pushed (not a git work tree, nothing to commit, push rejected or offline).
errorCases.detection: commitAndPushArtifacts returns committed false or pushed false with a reason.
errorCases.response: The item's status is unchanged; TrackerOutcome.docs carries committed, pushed and the reason. A push that failed leaves the commit local.
errorCases.userImpact: The result says the documents are not on the remote yet and why; links from the GitHub item resolve once they are pushed.

errorCases.scenario: The GitHub issue was created but the ref could not be written back to the artifact.
errorCases.detection: For an issue record, createBugfixTrackerIssue returns 'created' with the reason 'ref-unrecorded'; for a story, the write of meta.tracker throws after the create call returned a ref.
errorCases.response: The outcome is 'failed' and names the created ref. No duplicate follows: the item carries its unique label, and the next approval or the backfill finds it by that label and adopts it, writing the ref then.
errorCases.userImpact: The user sees the ref and that it was not recorded; the next run repairs it.

errorCases.detection: approveWorkflowTarget wraps each artifact's tracker step in a try and catch.
errorCases.response: The outcome is 'failed' with the error's message. The approval of that artifact and of the rest of a batch continues.
errorCases.userImpact: One failed line in the result; nothing else is affected.

errorCases.scenario: The backfill stops part of the way through (a gh failure, or the daemon is stopped).
errorCases.detection: The backfill request returns the outcomes gathered so far, or the connection ends.
errorCases.response: Items already created keep their refs. Running the backfill again skips them and continues with the rest.
errorCases.userImpact: A partial result; a second run finishes the job without duplicates.

edgeCases.input: The setting is false for the repo.
edgeCases.expected: Every tracker step is 'skipped' with the reason that the setting is off; no gh call is made, not even the sign-in check.

edgeCases.input: A repo whose github.json entry says type 'none', after the one-time step at daemon start.
edgeCases.expected: Its setting was written as false, so every tracker step is skipped. Turning the setting on later tracks the repo, using its git remote: the one flag decides.

edgeCases.input: A repo with no entry in github.json and a GitHub remote.
edgeCases.expected: Tracked by default: the step's own lookup takes the target from the git remote and the default labels. resolveGithubConfig still returns 'none' for it, so the three other callers behave as before.

edgeCases.input: An artifact whose item is already on the tracker is approved again.
edgeCases.expected: 'already-exists' with its ref; nothing is created.

edgeCases.input: An LLD under an epic whose HLD was never pushed.
edgeCases.expected: 'skipped' with the existing reason that the epic is not on the tracker yet; the backfill creates the epic first and then the story.

edgeCases.input: A standalone story whose work item has an issue record that is already on the tracker.
edgeCases.expected: No second issue is created; the design is linked on the existing GitHub issue and the outcome is 'updated'.

edgeCases.input: A plan is approved and the tracker config has pushTasks false.
edgeCases.expected: The tasks are pushed: with the setting on, every item is tracked. pushTasks no longer decides.

edgeCases.input: A batch approval of several artifacts under one epic.
edgeCases.expected: One tracker outcome per approved artifact, run one after another in the order they were approved; withheld artifacts have none.

edgeCases.input: A DEF, SPEC, CR or EXT artifact is approved.
edgeCases.expected: No tracker outcome: these kinds are not tracker items.

edgeCases.input: The backfill meets a finished work item (its BUILD record is approved).
edgeCases.expected: Its GitHub issue is created and closed at once, with its tasks, so it does not appear as open work.

edgeCases.input: The backfill is run with the dry-run flag.
edgeCases.expected: It returns the list of items it would add, in order, and makes no gh call that changes anything.

edgeCases.input: An issue record that is not yet approved.
edgeCases.expected: Not pushed by the approval step or the backfill; it is pushed when it is approved.

edgeCases.input: A BUILD record is approved for a Story whose issue, story or tasks were never pushed.
edgeCases.expected: 'skipped' with the reason that there is nothing on the tracker to close; the backfill creates and closes it.

edgeCases.input: The TUI approves with withTracker false.
edgeCases.expected: No tracker step and no commit or push of the documents.

edgeCases.input: The working tree holds other uncommitted files when an item is approved.
edgeCases.expected: Only the approved artifact's files and its definition are added and committed; the other files are left as they are.

invariantsToPreserve.text: An approval is never failed or undone by the tracker: the stamp is written first and the tracker step only reports. The approval's response waits for the step, which is bounded by the timeout on each call.
The GitHub owner and repo never come from the default entry of the tracker config; only from the repo's own entry or its git remote.
A stored tracker ref means the item exists: no push function creates a second item for an artifact that already carries a ref.
The other-party review rule and the code-review gate decide whether an artifact is approved before any tracker step runs; a withheld artifact is never pushed.
gh is never run by a test and never by the model in the session; tracker functions take their gh calls as injected dependencies.
Every setting the plugins show comes from the config catalog and is written through config.write.
resolveGithubConfig and its three callers outside the tracker step behave exactly as before.
A work item's GitHub issue is closed by one piece of code only.

migration.stateBefore: Only the TUI approve service pushes to GitHub, and only for an HLD, an LLD under an epic and a plan. The in-chat approval and the plugins go through approveWorkflowTarget, which pushes nothing. An approved issue record never creates a GitHub issue and a standalone story cannot be pushed. A repo is tracked only when ~/.insrc/github.json has an entry for it or a default entry. No setting turns tracking on or off, and the steering tells the model to push an epic itself without saying when.
migration.stateAfter: One setting, on by default and adjustable per repo from both plugins, turns tracker pushing on or off. With it on and gh installed and signed in, one tracker step runs inside the approval on every path: it adds or updates issue records, epics, stories, standalone stories and tasks, closes them when the build is approved, and commits and pushes their documents. A repo with a GitHub remote is tracked without any entry in github.json; resolveGithubConfig and its other callers are unchanged. The approval result and the workflow's messages report the outcome, the steering tells the model the daemon does it, and a backfill has added the approved items that were never pushed and closed the finished ones.

migrationSteps.action: Add the tracker.addItems catalog row, its per-repo reader, and the one-time step at daemon start that writes the setting false for repos whose github.json entry says type 'none'. Nothing else reads the setting yet.
Add a timeout to the tracker's gh and git calls, and the shared test helper that installs a recording gh fake and a temp config path.

Add the tracker step: its checks in the order setting, target, gh installed, gh signed in; its handling of each kind, with the unique labels and the look-up-before-create; the close on a BUILD record; and the commit and push of the documents. Nothing calls it yet.

Call the tracker step from approveWorkflowTarget and return tracker[]; carry it through the daemon request and insrc_workflow_approve. In the same step, give the existing approval suites the shared helper so they make no gh call.
Make the TUI approve service asynchronous and replace its switch and its commit with the tracker step; change its interface and its two callers to await it.
Remove the close leg and its followOn entry from the bugfix follow-on, so the tracker step is the one owner of the close.

Add the tracker line to the pendingApproval block of insrc_workflow_step, and rewrite the tracker and bugfix guides in the steering source and the insrc_workflow_approve description; refresh the plugin copy of the steering source.
Show the setting on the VS Code and JetBrains settings pages: the default row from the catalog and the repo's own value in the per-repo section.
Add the backfill stream request with its dry run.

After the daemon is updated: run the backfill's dry run on this repo, show the list to the user, and on their go-ahead run it. Creating GitHub issues cannot be undone by reverting code; they can only be closed.
prerequisiteFlags: the user's go-ahead on the dry-run list

migration.backwardCompat: approveWorkflowTarget gains an optional field in its result and an optional test seam; its existing fields and decisions are unchanged. resolveGithubConfig and the three push functions keep their signatures and behaviour. Artifacts already on the tracker keep their refs and are never pushed again. Four things change for existing users. (1) The TUI approve service becomes asynchronous and its result's tracker field changes type and its commit field goes; its interface and two callers change with it. (2) A repo with a GitHub remote and no tracker config starts being tracked, and an in-chat approval now commits and pushes the approved documents, as the TUI already did; turning the setting off for the repo restores the old behaviour. (3) pushTasks, commitArtifacts and type 'none' in github.json no longer decide whether the tracker step pushes; repos that had type 'none' are given the setting false once, so they stay off. (4) The bugfix follow-on no longer reports 'bugfix-complete' in followOn; the close is reported in tracker[].

alternativesConsidered.name: Catalog setting with a per-repo override, one tracker step inside the approval
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A catalog row gives the default; a per-repo key overrides it; approveWorkflowTarget runs one tracker function for every artifact it approves.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add a catalog row tracker.addItems (boolean, default true) and a per-repo value stored under tracker.byRepo.<repoPath>.addItems in the same config file, read by one reader. Add one asynchronous function that, given an approved artifact, decides what to add, update or close in the tracker (issue record, epic, story, standalone story, tasks, completion), pushes the documents it refers to, and returns an outcome. approveWorkflowTarget awaits it for each approved artifact and returns the outcomes in a new tracker[] field; the TUI approve service awaits the same function in place of its own switch and its own commit. The plugins show the default row from the catalog and write the per-repo value for the open project.
pros: One place decides and one place pushes, on every approval path
The setting reaches both settings pages through the catalog they already render
Per-repo and default values follow the existing byRepo pattern
cons: approveWorkflowTarget gains a network side effect, and the daemon serves no other request while a gh call runs
The TUI approve service must become asynchronous
Each plugin needs code to write the per-repo value, not only the catalog row

alternativesConsidered.name: Per-repo flag in the tracker config file, new IPC for the plugins
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Store addItems on the repo's entry in github.json beside the other tracker settings and give the plugins a dedicated get and set request.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add an addItems field to GithubEntry and to the default entry in ~/.insrc/github.json, read by resolveGithubConfig. Add two daemon requests, one to read and one to write the flag for a repo, and a dedicated row on each plugin's settings page that uses them. The push logic is the same single function as in a1.
pros: All tracker settings stay in one file
The flag is truly per repo with no dynamic key
cons: The setting is outside the config catalog, so neither settings page shows it without bespoke UI and two new requests
A second settings mechanism to keep in step with the first
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Meets the requirements but needs a second settings mechanism (two new requests and bespoke rows in both plugins) for one boolean.

alternativesConsidered.name: Push from the daemon's approve handler only
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Keep the approval function free of side effects and run the tracker step in the daemon's workflow.approve handler, beside the bugfix follow-on.
alternativesConsidered.approach: The setting is stored as in a1. The tracker function is called from the 'workflow.approve' handler in the daemon after approveWorkflowTarget returns, and its outcomes are added to the result there. The TUI approve service keeps its own push.
pros: Sits beside the existing follow-on seam
cons: Two callers hold the push, the daemon handler and the TUI, and can drift again, which is the defect being fixed
Anything that calls approveWorkflowTarget directly does not push
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Leaves two callers holding the push. That split is why in-chat approvals stopped pushing; keeping it invites the same defect.
